data.description:
v0 of the job-search triage and application-assist CLI, per job-search-automation-v2.md (the spec; where it conflicts with instinct, ask before deviating). Deterministic Rust pipeline: ingest -> hard-filter gates -> scoring -> review queue -> apply package, over an append-only JSONL event log (source of truth) with an in-memory projection. The spec's Key Decisions section is settled - do not re-litigate.

Delivery workflow: one increment per PR; stacked PRs capped at 2; before opening a new stacked PR, check for review feedback (Copilot, Remi, human) on existing PRs and incorporate it.

Guardrails that apply to every pebble: no LLM/API calls in v0 (fully deterministic); never auto-submit without explicit per-job approval; never fabricate or embellish experience; never contact people automatically; never match blacklisted companies; be a good citizen (rate limits, ToS).

data.title: Increment 0: Design PR - event schema + command surface
data.description: Design-doc PR proposing the event schema (event types + payloads) and the CLI command surface, reviewed before any pipeline work begins. Must answer: (a) lead identity - what uniquely identifies a lead (URL? req id? title+company hash?) and re-ingest semantics for updated/reposted leads, including the ignore matching rule: a durable ignore mark means a re-ingested lead never re-enters the queue; (b) the full lifecycle in the event schema, including outcome events (lead_applied, lead_screened, ...) even though v0 emits only a subset; (c) the alpha's fate - fresh start vs one-time CSV import of ~/Documents/Job Hunt/events/events.csv; (d) review-queue interaction model - a prompt loop is plenty for v0; a ratatui TUI is a vNext-sized dependency. Also supersedes the placeholder lead open/list/close subcommands.

data.title: Increment 1: Ingest steel thread - drop-in adapter + JSONL event log + projection + TOML config
data.description: First end-to-end slice (the steel thread). gwl-jobs ingest <url|file>: fetch and extract main text (HTML and plain text only; PDF extraction is a separate follow-up pebble), best-effort structured fields (title, company, compensation, location, req id, source); v0 ships only the drop-in adapter (Greenhouse/Ashby/Lever are vNext). Emit lead_ingested with raw text + structured fields. Append-only JSONL event log is the source of truth; in-memory projection rebuilt on startup; gwl-jobs show <id> reads a lead back from the projection. TOML config: comp floor + ceiling, remote-only flag, blacklist, alias table, scoring weights, generic-letter path, target-companies list (empty for now). Design for (do not build) pluggable extension points: source adapters, scoring sources, cover-letter generation. Good citizen: 200-500ms delay between requests, obey control headers and redirects, respect ToS. Fully deterministic - no LLM/API calls.

data.title: Increment 2: Hard filter gates
data.description: Binary reject gates, not scored. A lead failing any gate is durably recorded via lead_rejected { gate, reason }. Gates: remote-only (reject non-remote); compensation floor (reject below configured floor; unknown/missing comp PASSES the floor gate - settled decision); blacklist (reject blacklisted companies - never match them); ideological red lines - the MECHANISM ships in v0 as a filter list, the CONTENT is deferred to the later LLM scorer (ship an empty list). Deterministic; no LLM.

data.title: Increment 3: Scoring engine
data.description: Per-dimension scores 0-100, each with a confidence field (default 1.0; only meaningful once LLM scorers arrive). Dimensions: level (title signals + quoted years-of-experience in the posting); skills (keyword overlap between JD and ~/Source/resume/resume.json skills, plus configurable alias table, e.g. K8s -> Kubernetes); compensation (linear interpolation floor->ceiling; at/above ceiling = 100; unknown/missing comp drops the dimension out of the composite with weight renormalization, noted in the breakdown). Composite = weighted sum (Sum(wi*si)/Sum(wi)), default equal weights, configurable via TOML. Breakdown must be human-readable, e.g. 75 = 0.3*level(80) + 0.3*skills(90) + 0.4*comp(60), so ranking decisions are debuggable. Emit lead_scored. Deterministic; no LLM.

data.title: Increment 4: Interactive review queue
data.description: Review queue ranked by composite score; interactive CLI prompt loop (ratatui TUI is vNext per the design PR). Queue shows a deferral count per lead (number of times marked no-action). Marks: apply-automatically (this mark IS the approval - no second confirmation; the final browser click is expected and fine); apply-manual (user takes personal action; tool facilitates); no-action (stays in queue, reappears next review, deferral count increments); ignore (durable - a re-ingested ignored lead never re-enters the queue; enforce at ingest time against the projection, per the matching rule specified in Increment 0). Emit lead_reviewed; marks are latest-wins projections over lead_reviewed events (re-marking emits a new event).

data.title: Increment 5: Apply package
data.description: apply-automatically: assemble the full package - generic cover letter (config path) + generated answers cheat sheet (common ATS questions -> resume-derived answers from ~/Source/resume/resume.json, rendered and displayed alongside; the question list is a static list in config or code - do not invent it ad hoc; nothing is auto-filled in v0) + resume PDF; emit lead_apply_queued; open the posting URL. Degrades to manual submit in v0 (Playwright autofill is vNext). apply-manual: provide the JD + resume context + the same cheat sheet. Guardrails: never auto-submit without explicit per-job approval (the mark is that approval; final click is the user's); never fabricate or embellish experience; never contact people automatically; never send resume data to an unapproved service (moot in v0 - no API calls); no cover-letter generation in v0.

data.description: Extend the drop-in ingest adapter to extract main text from PDF files (spec: URL or file - HTML/PDF/text). data.title: Application automation
data.description: vNext: automate the apply path. Playwright autofill (shell out to Python) and cover-letter generation. See docs/specs/job-search-automation-v2.md vNext Backlog.

data.title: Smarter matching & finding
data.description: vNext: improve lead quality - find more (source adapters) and score better (ideological alignment, semantic matching, bonus/malus). See docs/specs/job-search-automation-v2.md vNext Backlog.

data.title: Playwright autofill + open browser
data.description: Shell out to a Python Playwright script to autofill an ATS application form from resume.json and the answers cheat sheet, then open the browser for the user to click the final Apply. Target: correct autofill, user clicks final Apply (not fully autonomous submission). Degrades gracefully: full autofill where possible, else pre-filled answers and open URL. Respect ToS; skip sites where automation violates ToS. Top of the vNext backlog.

data.title: Cover-letter generation
data.description: Generate tailored cover letters using the human-written corpus (~/Documents/Job Hunt/cover/) as the style guide. Never write from scratch - the corpus is the style guide (settled guardrail). LLM-based (vNext; v0 uses a generic letter).

data.title: Greenhouse/Ashby/Lever source adapters
data.description: Add pluggable source adapters for Greenhouse, Ashby, and Lever public JSON APIs (no scraping; ToS-friendly), plus a configurable company watchlist (target-companies list in TOML config, currently empty). Poll for new postings matching filters. Good citizen: 200-500ms delay between requests, obey control headers and redirects, client-side caching for cacheable data.

data.title: Ideological alignment via Remi
data.description: Add an ideological-alignment scoring dimension via the persistent agent Remi (LLM scorer). This is the deferred content for the ideological-red-line filter mechanism shipped in v0 (empty list). Design for pluggable scoring sources; the confidence field on scores becomes meaningful here.

data.title: Semantic skills matching
data.description: Add semantic skills matching via embeddings (small local model) as an additional scoring source, catching paraphrases keyword match misses (e.g., distributed systems vs microservices). Drop-in behind the Scorer interface; v0 keyword + alias table remains the baseline.

data.title: Bonus/malus attribute scores
data.description: Add configurable bonus/malus score adjustments for certain attributes (e.g., +N for target companies, -N for certain signals). Config-driven, deterministic. Extends the weighted-sum composite.

data.title: SQLite projection
data.description: Add a SQLite projection (read model) over the JSONL event log for ad-hoc querying (e.g., show ignored jobs, applied in last 30 days). The JSONL event log remains the source of truth; SQLite is a derived cache rebuilt by replaying the log. Deferred from v0 (in-memory projection is sufficient for a single-user CLI).

data.title: Markdown export of leads
data.description: gwl-jobs export: render leads (JD text, extracted metadata, marks/outcomes) as durable, greppable, LLM-ingestible markdown files - matching Grey's existing alpha-corpus habit (~/Documents/Job Hunt/events/jds/), which was built for search and for Remi to read. Markdown is an EXPORT format for this tool, not an input (see GWLJ-evnuay's close reason). Design when vNext LLM features land; the JSONL log is the source of truth, markdown is a rendering.

data.title: Local-model remote/work-arrangement classifier
data.description: Replace the v0 keyword heuristics for the remote field (src/ingest/extract.rs detect_remote, negation-aware) with a small local model classifying work arrangement: remote / hybrid / on-site / unknown, producing remote: Option<bool> plus confidence (< 1.0, which the scoring composite already carries). Feeds the remote-only gate (Increment 2) and the remote scoring dimension (Increment 3). Deferral is safe by design: the field contract (Option<bool> + confidence) does not change when the detector improves. Same local-model infrastructure as semantic skills matching.

Binary reject gates, not scored. A lead failing any gate is durably recorded via rejected { gate, reason }. Gates: remote-only (reject only CONFIDENT non-remote: remote=Some(false), broadened to explicit hybrid/on-site/in-office/must-be-located patterns even when 'remote' is mentioned; remote=None passes to review - false rejections are invisible losses, false passes cost one glance; queue flags 'remote unknown' in Increment 4); compensation floor (reject below configured floor; unknown/missing comp PASSES the floor gate - settled decision); blacklist (reject blacklisted companies - never match them); ideological red lines - the MECHANISM ships in v0 as a filter list, the CONTENT is deferred to the later LLM scorer (ship an empty list). Deterministic; no LLM.

Per-dimension scores 0-100, each with a confidence field (default 1.0; only meaningful once LLM scorers arrive). Dimensions: level (title signals + quoted years-of-experience in the posting); skills (keyword overlap between JD and ~/Source/resume/resume.json skills, plus configurable alias table, e.g. K8s -> Kubernetes); compensation (linear interpolation floor->ceiling; at/above ceiling = 100; unknown/missing comp drops the dimension out of the composite with weight renormalization, noted in the breakdown). Composite = weighted sum (Sum(wi*si)/Sum(wi)), default equal weights, configurable via TOML. Breakdown must be human-readable, e.g. 75 = 0.3*level(80) + 0.3*skills(90) + 0.4*comp(60), so ranking decisions are debuggable. Emit scored. Deterministic; no LLM. FOURTH DIMENSION (confirmed 2026-08-26): remote - Some(true) -> 100, None -> 50 (middle), Some(false) never reaches scoring (gated). Weight via scoring_weights.remote, default equal; breakdown shows it (e.g. 82 = 0.25*level(80) + ... + 0.25*remote(100)). This is how positive remote signals bubble to the top of the review queue.

data.title: Pass-marker event: design conversation for torn-rejection edge
data.description: Design conversation to have when scoring lands (related to GWLJ-1hp1r6). Known limit of the batch-prefix crash policy (design doc 0001 section 1): if a snapshot event persists but its following rejected event is torn away, the lead presents as gate-passing until the next re-ingest. The full fix is an explicit pass-marker event (or treating scored as that marker). Decide then: add an 'evaluated' event, or accept scored-as-marker, or accept the edge. Do not invent mid-increment - this is the reminder to have the conversation.

data.title: Logging: file sink + configurable level (default error)
data.description: Land the logging story before Increment 3 (scoring). User-facing utility: no tracing log lines on stdout/stderr by default. Config: log_level (default 'error'), log_file (optional; default <data_dir>/gwl-jobs.log). CLI: --log-level overrides config. Precedence: CLI > config > RUST_LOG > error. fmt layer writes to the file (append, no rotation); miette errors still go to stderr (error reporting, not logging). --telemetry on keeps the OTLP layer; fmt moves from stderr to the file. Implies hoisting Config::load to main (before subscriber init) and passing &Config down to commands. See docs/decisions/0005-logging.md.

data.title: Application state machine commands (outcome + transitions)
data.description: Complete coverage of the application/interview state machine in CLI commands. Non-terminal transitions: gwl-jobs applied [--method], gwl-jobs screened [--contact], gwl-jobs interviewed [--stage], gwl-jobs offered. Terminal outcomes: gwl-jobs outcome <lead> <accepted|rejected_by_employer|withdrawn|declined|unresponsive|archived> [--note] [--at]. Adds 'unresponsive' to the outcome schema (design amendment — tracked separately because ghosting reflects negatively on the company for future interactions). Projection tracks the current state (latest outcome). All commands accept --at for retro-dating. See design doc 0001 §3/§8.

data.title: State machine transition validation (follow-up)
data.description: Enforce valid application-process transitions in the state machine commands (GWLJ-w8bofg). Refuse out-of-order events: interviewed before applied, offered before interviewed, terminal outcomes before applied, etc. v0 ships complete coverage without validation; this follow-up adds the state-machine enforcement. See design doc 0001 §3.

data.text: Sequencing: next step after Increment 3 (PR #7) merges; coupled to Increment 4's projection work (queue membership keys on outcomes).

Close reason, surfaced for visibility (recorded in the 2026-08-27 close event, which 'pb show' does not display): NOT NEEDED — the alpha markdown corpus (~/Documents/Job Hunt/events/jds/) is Grey's durable searchable store and Remi's reading material — markdown is an EXPORT format, not tool input. No bulk import is planned (fresh start, decision 0001), and real file drops will always identify the company. The empty-card concern is moot on that path; worst case the review card shows raw_text by design. Consequence for reviewers: markdown-as-input findings (e.g. the PR #7 note on '#' heading markers in the plain-text title heuristic) review against a superseded premise — markdown input is not a workflow. If plain-text drops ever become a real workflow, re-open or re-file. See also GWLJ-qito0d (markdown export of leads).

data.title: extract_years: leftmost-match semantics (follow-up)
data.description: extract_years uses leftmost-match: with multiple year mentions ('2 years of Kubernetes; 10+ years overall experience'), the leftmost (2) wins — arbitrary. Also matches year figures in non-experience contexts. Decide the fix direction (max? proximity to 'experience'?) and implement. Flagged in k3 review round 2 of PR #7.
